subject: Regional connectivity fluctuation affecting hosted API — Arcadia
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir.rao@arcadiahealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Arcadia SRE <sre@arcadiahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Slow inference and intermittent 500s for Arcadia regional cluster

Morning Marissa,

We're seeing a spike in 500 responses and a noticeable increase in tail latency from servers using the hosted API for our US-West region starting ~08:45 PT. Error rates have been spiking to ~7% and a few of our batch jobs timed out. We don't see anything obvious on our side and wanted to check if you have any ongoing degraded behavior in US-West.

Example: /v1/generate calls returning 500 with body: "upstream error: connection reset". Attached is a brief snippet of failed request IDs and timestamps.

Can you confirm if this is a known issue and an ETA for mitigation? This is impacting a small set of scheduled clinical reports.

Thanks,
Samir Rao
SRE, Arcadia Health
Attachments: arcadia-failed-ids-0618.csv (csv)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir.rao@arcadiahealth.com>
Cc: Arcadia SRE <sre@arcadiahealth.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Slow inference and intermittent 500s for Arcadia regional cluster

Hi Samir,

Thanks for the report and the sample IDs — that's helpful. We are seeing a regional connectivity fluctuation impacting a subset of hosts in US-West which is causing upstream connection resets and elevated token latency. Our on-call SREs have opened incident RW-20260618-US-WEST and we've posted an initial advisory on the status page (link below).

Immediate actions we've taken:
- Identified a networking fabric congestion event affecting a GPU host pool; traffic has been re-routed away from the impacted hosts.
- Enabled conservative request-level retries at the edge for affected routes to reduce customer-visible 500s.
- Spun up additional warm capacity in a nearby AZ to absorb burst traffic.

Observable impact: intermittent 500s and tail latency for ~5% of requests to US-West between 08:40–10:00 PT. We expect the re-routing to gradually reduce errors; full stabilization targeted by 12:00 PT.

Could you confirm whether your jobs see immediate improvement after retried attempts? If you can share 2–3 failing request IDs (or allow us to pull the IDs you sent), we'll cross-check traces and include them in the post-incident follow-up.

Status page: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/RW-20260618-US-WEST

I'll keep you updated as we make progress — apologies for the disruption.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Attachments: impact-matrix-arcadia-0618.csv (csv)

Subject: Arcadia: US-West connectivity fluctuation — request for traces and next steps

Ben / Lauren,

Looping you in — Arcadia reported customer-visible 500s and tail latency for US-West. Incident RW-20260618-US-WEST is open. Quick summary:
- Symptoms: intermittent upstream connection resets, ~5–7% error rate on /v1/generate for Arcadia's tenant, spike starting ~08:40 PT.
- Mitigation in progress: traffic re-route + request-level retries + warm capacity from adjacent AZ.
- Current ETA to stabilise: 12:00 PT (monitoring shows gradual improvement but some hosts still flapping).

Action items:
1) Ben — please prioritize a cross-check of host-level NIC errors and kernel logs for the impacted GPU pool (host group gw-usw-3). Look for buffer drops or link flaps between 08:30–10:30 PT.
2) Lauren — can you confirm whether the on-edge retry policy we enabled may affect Arcadia's idempotency assumptions? If needed, we'll include guidance in the customer update.
3) I'll coordinate with Arcadia to get failing request IDs and compile traces; attach diagnostic-traces-arcadia-0618.txt when ready.

I attached an initial impact matrix and the sample IDs they provided. Let's aim for one consolidated external update at ~15:30 PT with remediation details and next steps.

Thanks,
Marissa
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Update — US-West routing incident (RW-20260618-US-WEST) — mitigation and follow-up

Hi Samir,

Quick status update and follow-up from our incident:

What happened:
- A networking fabric congestion event in our US-West GPU host pool caused intermittent connection resets and elevated tail latency for a subset of customers (including Arcadia) between ~08:40–11:45 PT.

What we did to mitigate:
- Re-routed traffic off impacted hosts and drained affected instances.
- Enabled conservative request-level retries at the edge to reduce visible 500s while avoiding duplicate side effects.
- Cold-started additional warm capacity in an adjacent AZ to handle burst traffic.
- Replaced two NICs showing repeated link-flap patterns.

Customer impact:
- Approximate window: 08:40–11:45 PT; peak error rate ~7%.
- You may have seen increased latency and a small number of 500 responses. We do not see evidence of data loss.

Follow-up and next steps for Arcadia:
- We've attached the compiled traces and host-level diagnostics: diagnostic-traces-arcadia-0618.txt.
- Our postmortem is scheduled for Wednesday, 2026-06-23; we'll share a write-up including root cause analysis, timeline, and permanent mitigations.
- If you saw any job-level duplicates that you suspect were caused by retries, please send IDs and we'll correlate and assist with reconciliation.

Status page & incident link: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/RW-20260618-US-WEST
Shared folder with artifacts: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/shared/arcadia-incident-0618

Apologies again for the disruption. If you want a sync call to walk through the traces and timeline, I can set up a 30-minute window tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
